title: OpenCode wake re-injection gap and fix design
summary: The opencode ScheduleWakeup substrate only ARMS a wake (detached sleeper writes ORCH_SCHEDULED_TASK to <data>/wake/<session>.fire); nothing reads it back into the opencode session, so the orchestrator heartbeat ticks once then stalls. This refines note-mqixlv43mmd's "ScheduleWakeup-compatible scheduler = parity" claim — that covered arming only, not delivery. FIX design (in-plugin, no port discovery): packages/opencode-plugin/zonoid.ts receives client: OpencodeClient (@opencode-ai/sdk) in its factory input; the SDK exposes client.session.promptAsync({path:{id:sessionId}, body:{parts:[{type:'text',text:prompt}]}}) which maps to POST /session/:id/prompt_async (204, no-wait). Add a per-session .fire watcher (cancel-then-arm, one per session) that parses the ORCH_SCHEDULED_TASK JSON payload and calls client.session.promptAsync with the prompt. Arm the watcher from the schedule_wakeup tool execute (ctx.sessionID available). Structural reference: lib/codex-wakeup-delivery.js + adapters/codex/wakeup-monitor.js (codex uses external `codex resume`; opencode does it in-plugin via the SDK client). opencode server port is dynamic and not published to a file, so the in-process SDK client path is strongly preferred over an external HTTP monitor.
